thread:
maria: Heads-up — customer reported missing tenant_id in S3-delivered audit batches (private deployment, presigned PUTs). Some files show audit_schema 1 while others look like 2. Any ideas?

ingrid: I hit something similar in staging last week — multipart uploads via presigned URLs can lose object metadata headers. Not all SDKs preserve x-amz-meta-* across parts.

jakob: interesting. multipart shouldn't rewrite metadata on complete, but presigned flows sometimes use an intermediate service that strips headers. Are they using SSE-KMS with presigned PUTs or standard PutObject?

maria: they said SSE-KMS. Sample simplified payload they see: 
```json
{
  "event_type":"audit.auth",
  "tenant_id": null,
  "actor":"user:alice",
  "audit_schema": 1,
  "payload": {"action":"login"}
}
```

samir: quick hypothesis: our batching/flush path offloads very large event bodies to S3 and writes a pointer object. If the pointer write happens via presigned multipart, the rehydration code expects tenant_id in object metadata but some SDKs drop it, so we end up writing null into the reconstructed event.

security-ops: can someone capture repro steps and object metadata? also flag — KMS headers matter here (x-amz-server-side-encryption, x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id). Some clients omit them on parts which may cause a different behavior.

ingrid: repro plan: create a >3MB JSON event, upload via presigned multipart from a minimal python client, inspect HEAD/GET metadata and our ingestion logs. will post script shortly.

jakob: proposed short-term mitigation: require minimal routing fields inside the JSON body (not only in object metadata). Schema change: audit_v -> string and tenant_id must be present at root. That way presigned uploads losing metadata won't lose routing. We'll call it audit_v: "2".

maria: agreed. This is a customer-impacting schema change but it's backwards compatible if we accept both v1 and v2. We should add an ingestion validation that rejects objects missing tenant_id in both metadata and body and sends them to a quarantine bucket + alert.

samir: I'll own the ingestion validation + quarantine flow. Also add a deterministic log line when we auto-quarantine for easier triage: `quarantine_reason=missing_tenant_id source=ingest.s3 object_key=<key>`.

audit-bot: NOTE: migration implications — customers using S3 export with presigned multipart must either embed tenant_id in body or switch to signed PutObject w/ server-side headers. We'll need a delivery contract addendum and a flag in onboarding.

maria: action items:
- ingrid: repro script + failing object (ETA today)
- jakob: draft schema v2 with required root fields + sample payloads (ETA tomorrow)
- samir: implement ingestion validation + quarantine + log signal (ETA next week)
- security-ops: onboarding doc updates + customer advisory draft (ETA 48h)

samir: small add-on — check signed URL expiry too. If presigned PUT expires and client retries with a new signed url that omits metadata, we could end up with mixed schema files. Also check S3 partitioning logic: object_key patterns should include tenant scoping (prefixed path) to reduce cross-tenant risk.

ingrid: pasted repro gist: https://gist.github.com/xxxx (script demonstrates HEAD metadata missing after multipart complete).

maria: filing ENGSEC-4521 with attachments & initial logs. Will include sample object key and a small set of anonymized events.

security-ops: SOC note — when we auto-quarantine make sure RBAC is clear: only security+owner+audit-admins can see quarantined payloads. Don't expose raw tenant-less events broadly.

maria: scheduling a quick sync in 30m in #eng-security in case early fixes are needed. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
